open_points.subject: project-create replay after anonymisation
open_points.text: A01 rule 8 says a create after anonymisation with the former request id “is a new create, answered with the new record it made”, while the project-create rules refuse a customer reference that is unknown, erased, restricted or ended, and A04 applies the ordinary checks once the call is no longer recognised as a repeat.
open_points.question: When the former request id makes the call a new create but its submitted facts now fail an ordinary create check, is it refused or must it make and answer a new record?
options: Treat it as an ordinary new create and refuse it when any current create precondition fails.
Always make the new record after request-id removal, notwithstanding a current create refusal condition.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an ordinary new create and refuse it when a current precondition fails.

witness.initial: Customer C is eligible. Project P naming C was created with request id K, then archived and anonymised, removing K and P's customer link.
events: The owner resubmits P's original create request with request id K and customer reference C.
outcomes: A01 rule 8 is read categorically: Registry creates and answers a new project.
The normal create checks apply because K is no longer a repeat: Registry refuses the restricted customer reference and creates nothing.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a newly created project or a refusal; the catalogue and audit log also differ.

open_points.subject: replacement of an uploaded import file after confirmation
open_points.text: A21 now lists “re-uploads replacing a confirmed file” as covered. A16 says another upload replaces the kept file “one of the same bytes included” and requires an old confirmation to be refused even when the new file has the same bytes, but A13 binds the confirmation to the file only by its digest and does not say that an upload clears the pending confirmation.
open_points.question: How does Registry distinguish replacement by an identical upload so that the old confirmation is refused: must every accepted upload invalidate the pending confirmation, or may the old confirmation remain valid when the digest and all bound inputs are unchanged?
options: Every accepted re-upload invalidates or replaces the pending confirmation, including an identical-byte upload.
The old confirmation remains valid when the replacement has the same digest and the other bound inputs are unchanged.
open_points.default_guess: Clear the pending confirmation on every accepted upload.

witness.initial: One owner session has uploaded import file F and has a pending confirmation bound to digest(F), the picks and mapping inputs; no migration closure exists.
events: The owner uploads the identical bytes F again in the same session.
The owner submits the still-pending confirmation value with the same picks and mapping inputs.
outcomes: A16's replacement rule and required test are followed: the submission is refused because the file confirmed earlier is no longer kept.
A13's stated binding is followed: the pending value still exists, the new file has the same digest, all inputs match, and the import is accepted.
witness.observer: The owner sees refusal versus successful import, and the production store either remains unchanged or gains the imported records and migration closure.
